He occasionally conversed with Nell on his veranda, teased her about her teaching methods, and allowed young Robin to help him haul dulse. During a severe lightning storm, Nutmeg was killed when a strike hit the kitchen chimney and overturned the cage, leaving Mr. Pettifer grieving. Shortly after, a joke newspaper entry prompted his estranged wife, Emily, to arrive in Brierley, where they reconciled and resumed living together. unit: Following the death of her mother, Mary Farrow, Lucy and her twin brother Robin were taken in by Thirza Abernethy to live at Grey Shutters. Upon their arrival, Lucy immediately distinguished herself through her polite manners and immaculate appearance, though her brother frequently tormented her by pulling her hair, taking her food, or tricking her into dangerous misadventures, such as locking her in a toolhouse or urging her onto a pigpen fence. She began attending local Sunday school, where she memorized hymns and verses submissively, and helped diligently with small tasks around the farm. When school opened, she was enrolled as a pupil under Nell, sitting provisionally alongside Mirabel Cotton, who terrified her with tales of a deceased roaming uncle until Nell intervened. unit: Following the death of her mother, Mary Farrow, Lucy and her twin brother Robin were taken in by Thirza Abernethy to live at Grey Shutters. Upon their arrival, Lucy immediately distinguished herself through her polite manners and immaculate appearance, though her brother frequently tormented her by pulling her hair, taking her food, or tricking her into dangerous misadventures, such as locking her in a toolhouse or urging her onto a pigpen fence. She began attending local Sunday school, where she memorized hymns and verses submissively, and helped diligently with small tasks around the farm. When school opened, she was enrolled as a pupil under Nell, sitting provisionally alongside Mirabel Cotton, who terrified her with tales of a deceased roaming uncle until Nell intervened.
